summary.headline: Concord Biotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to Rs 309.1 crore, but gross margin fell about 400 bps to 76.2%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs 309.1 crore and H1 grew 26% to Rs 566.6 crore, with API up 30% and formulations up 6%. Gross margin contracted about 400 bps to 76.2% on solvent and raw material cost increases, while reported EBITDA margin was 33.8% (33.0% for H1). Management attributed the weak formulation line to customers shifting to buying API and to business moving from Advergent to the US subsidiary Stellon. Injectables (Unit IV) and Stellon are still ramping, and management guided to contract wins in H2 and a 38-40% medium-term EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; margin vs 33.2% in H1 FY26
+19% YoY; ex-JV share Rs 126.7 crore vs Rs 103.2 crore (+23%)

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 250.1 crore, +30% YoY; domestic API +42% and export +8% (reported), with deemed exports said to be materially higher. Growth led by anti-infectives, antifungals and oncology; immunosuppressants grew high double digits.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 58.9 crore, +6% YoY; domestic formulations +29%. Weakness attributed to customers buying API instead of finished formulations in emerging markets and to business moving from Advergent to Stellon.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Revenue nearly doubled YoY in H1 FY27, helped by Romidepsin and Everolimus.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: One commercial project; the opportunity under discussion is about $2 million annually, per management. Contract manufacturing for third parties is not classed as CDMO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth expected to be slightly better than the historical 18-19% CAGR, based on H1 growth of 26% and Q3 visibility.
Medium-term EBITDA margin expected in the 38-40% range once Stellon and injectables ramp; reported margin currently 33-34%.
Full-year gross margin recovery expected as solvent and power costs normalise; management expects the gross margin trajectory to return to historical levels.
Stellon expected to contribute meaningfully from H2 FY27; formulation contracts for injectables expected in H2.
Capex guidance: maintenance capex Rs 20-30 crore a year; growth capex about Rs 50-60 crore in each of FY27 and FY28 (Rs 100-120 crore total).
Effective tax rate 24-25% for the rest of FY27 and FY28.
Injectables TAM about Rs 5,000 crore; management sees about Rs 300 crore top line from injectables over 3-4 years if large customers come on board.
capex_capacity: Unit I utilisation 75%; Unit III (Limbasi) 55%; Unit II (oral solid, Valthera) 21%; Unit IV (Stellon injectables) 5%.
USFDA inspection of Unit II formulation facility completed in H1 FY27; ANVISA approval received for Unit III Limbasi.
Several customer audits of the injectables facility completed in recent months; contracts expected to materialise in H2.
Gross margin benefit from in-house injectables not yet visible; intra-company API transfers are priced at market rather than cost, so low utilisation can weigh on gross margin.
Renewable energy investment made last year is expected to lower power and fuel costs once they stabilise.
demand_pricing: Immunosuppressant growth driven by share gains and second-source wins, with market growth of about 10%; key markets are the US, Latin America and Japan.
Pipeline of 10-15 products in development on top of about 30 commercial fermentation-based APIs; Nystatin US validation quantities have been supplied and commercial supply has not yet begun.
Fusidic acid being launched in emerging markets and then global markets; Fidaxomicin US DMF filed.
Management says there has been no pricing pressure; Concord has won share by offering significant price discounts to customers' existing suppliers.
Raw material cost increases (solvents) have not been passed on to customers; management says the rise is short-term and will be addressed through R&D and productivity.
Inspira dermatology division launched in the last couple of months; India dermatology market for the product range about Rs 5,000 crore; target of Rs 400-500 crore revenue in 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the API growth sustainable at a mid-teens rate, and what are the key products and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to build on the historical 18-19% API growth, with additional upside from injectables, CDMO and finished formulations. Growth is driven by anti-infectives, antifungals and oncology, with new customer additions.

qa_highlights.question: What are the utilisation rates for Unit II and the injectables unit, and what are the timelines for injectables contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit II is at 21% and the injectables Unit IV at 5%. Several customer audits have been completed and contracts are expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the effective tax rate change?
qa_highlights.answer: The tax rate is expected to be 24-25% for the rest of FY27 and FY28, with no unusual items.

qa_highlights.question: Has pricing changed in Q2, and have raw material costs been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: No pricing pressure; Concord offered price discounts to win customers. Raw material cost increases have not been passed on, as management sees them as short-term.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company revisit its FY27 growth guidance given H1 growth of 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management still expects FY27 growth slightly above the historical 18%, with reasonable visibility into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-term EBITDA margin is seen at 38-40% once Stellon and injectables ramp. Capex is Rs 20-30 crore maintenance a year plus Rs 50-60 crore growth capex in each of FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO revenue and what is the gross margin mix impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The CDMO opportunity is about $2 million annually from one commercial project. Gross margin pressure was mainly from raw material prices, with a smaller product-mix effect. API:formulation split is about 80:20.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell about 400 bps YoY to 76.2%; full-year recovery depends on solvent and power costs easing.
Injectables Unit IV at 5% utilisation and Stellon still at an early stage; H2 contract conversion is not yet confirmed.
Formulation growth at 6% lags API at 30%; customers shifting to API purchase could persist.
Customers shifting procurement to Indian subsidiaries, so export and domestic revenue splits are hard to read.
Concord cites margin recovery to 38-40% over the next few years, but reported EBITDA is currently 33-34%.
Pending US validation for Nystatin and FDA approvals for files could drive future volume growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and visibility, but defensive on margins and formulations. Management repeatedly attributed margin pressure to temporary raw material and power costs and explained the formulation shortfall through customer procurement shifts, while H2 injectables and Stellon contracts remained unconfirmed.
key_quotes: Revenues for Q2 FY ‘27 grew 25% year -on-year.

adds.what: Unit IV Stellon injectables facility (currently 5% utilised, ramping)

growth.why: FY27 growth guided slightly better than the historical 18% CAGR (held), backed by H1 revenue +26% and Q3 visibility; delivery relies on Unit IV injectables contracts expected in H2 (audits done, no signed numbers given) and share gains in immunosuppressants, so backing is partial rather than order-book clear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell about 400 bps to 76.2% in Q2 on solvent and raw material costs, and reported EBITDA margin is 33.8%; management targets 38-40% medium-term, but Unit IV is at 5% utilisation and gross margin benefit from injectables is not yet visible.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unit IV (Stellon injectables) is ramping from 5% utilisation and growth capex of Rs 50-60 crore a year is planned for FY27 and FY28, so new capacity is coming online, though its utilisation is still very low.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue grew 26% to Rs 566.6 crore, API grew 30% in Q2 to Rs 250.1 crore, and management guides FY27 growth slightly above the historical 18-19% CAGR with Q3 visibility.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has already set Rs 100-120 crore total capex across FY27 and FY28 (Rs 20-30 crore maintenance plus Rs 50-60 crore growth a year), with Unit II at 21% and Unit IV at 5% utilisation, so a further sizable announcement is less likely in the near term.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth is guided slightly above the 18% historical rate after H1 growth of 26%, but management held guidance rather than raising it, and the H2 contract conversion is unconfirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin fell about 400 bps to 76.2%, formulations grew only 6%, and the H2 injectables and Stellon contracts remain unsigned, so a margin or formulation miss could force a cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Injectables contracts are expected in H2 after audits, Fusidic acid is launching in emerging markets, Fidaxomicin US DMF is filed, Nystatin commercial supply has not started, and Inspira dermatology launched in the last couple of months with a Rs 400-500 crore target over 4-5 years.

rows.label: Injectables contracts from Stellon Unit IV
rows.why: Several customer audits are complete and contracts are expected in H2, with management building in about Rs 300 crore top line over 3-4 years if large customers come on board, though no signed numbers were given.

rows.label: Nystatin US commercial supply
rows.why: US validation quantities have been supplied but commercial supply has not started, and it depends on pending US validation.

rows.label: Solvent and power cost normalisation
rows.why: Management expects gross margin to return to historical levels as solvent and power costs normalise and the renewable energy investment lowers power and fuel costs, but raw material increases have not been passed on to customers.

tone.note: Management was confident on API demand and FY27 growth visibility but defensive on the 400 bps gross margin drop and weak formulations, which it blamed on temporary solvent and power costs and customers buying API; analysts pushed on margin recovery and unconfirmed injectables contracts.
